results.title: Atoms of a proposition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The atoms of a proposition $A$ form the finite set of atoms occurring in $A$: an atom $x$ has the single atom $x$, and the atoms of $B \wedge C$, $B \vee C$ and $B \to C$ are the atoms of $B$ together with the atoms of $C$.

results.title: The truth value depends only on the atoms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If two Boolean valuations $v$ and $w$ agree on every atom of a proposition $A$, then $A$ has the same truth-table value under $v$ as under $w$.

results.title: Substituting a truth value for an atom
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an atom $p$, a Boolean $b$ and a proposition $A$, the proposition $A[p := b]$ is obtained from $A$ by replacing every occurrence of the atom $p$ by the constant $\top$, written $\bot \to \bot$, if $b$ is true, and by $\bot$ if $b$ is false.

results.title: Boolean quantification over an atom
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an atom $p$ and a proposition $A$, the Boolean quantification $\exists p.\, A$ is the disjunction $A[p := \top] \vee A[p := \bot]$, where $A[p := \top]$ and $A[p := \bot]$ replace the atom $p$ in $A$ by the constant $\top = (\bot \to \bot)$ and by $\bot$ respectively.

results.title: Boolean quantification over a list of atoms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list of atoms $p_1, \dots, p_n$ and a proposition $A$, the iterated Boolean quantification $\exists p_1 \cdots p_n.\, A$ is $\exists p_1.\, \exists p_2.\, \cdots \exists p_n.\, A$: $A$ is quantified over $p_n$ first and over $p_1$ last, and for the empty list the result is $A$ itself.

results.title: Truth of a Boolean quantification over a list of atoms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p_1, \dots, p_n$ be a list of atoms that does not contain $\bot$, let $A$ be a proposition and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation with $v(\bot)$ false. Then the iterated Boolean quantification $\exists p_1 \cdots p_n.\, A$ is true under $v$ if and only if $A$ is true under some valuation $w$ that agrees with $v$ on every atom not in the list.

results.title: Craig interpolation, semantic form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be propositions such that every Boolean valuation $v$ with $v(\bot)$ false that makes $A$ true also makes $B$ true. Then there is a proposition $I$ whose atoms all lie among the atoms common to $A$ and $B$ together with $\bot$, such that every valuation $v$ with $v(\bot)$ false that makes $A$ true makes $I$ true, and every valuation $v$ with $v(\bot)$ false that makes $I$ true makes $B$ true.

results.title: Craig interpolation for classical natural deduction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be propositions such that $A \to B$ is derivable without assumptions in classical propositional logic $\mathrm{CPL}$ (natural deduction with the axioms $\neg\neg C \to C$). Then there is a proposition $I$ whose atoms all lie among the atoms common to $A$ and $B$ together with $\bot$, such that $A \to I$ and $I \to B$ are both derivable without assumptions in $\mathrm{CPL}$.

results.title: The multiplication dual is a colon quotient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $K$ a field that is an $A$-algebra, and write $1$ for the $A$-submodule $A \cdot 1$ of $K$. For every $A$-submodule $M$ of $K$, the dual submodule of $M$ with respect to the multiplication form $(x, y) \mapsto xy$ on $K$ equals the quotient $1 / M$, the set of $x \in K$ with $xy \in A \cdot 1$ for all $y \in M$.

results.title: Multiplication is a nondegenerate bilinear form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $K$, the $K$-bilinear form $(x, y) \mapsto xy$ on $K$ is nondegenerate: if $xy = 0$ for all $y \in K$ then $x = 0$, and if $xy = 0$ for all $x \in K$ then $y = 0$.

Then the $A$-linear map $M^\vee \to \operatorname{Hom}_A(M, A)$ sending $x$ to the functional $y \mapsto xy$ on $M$ is surjective.

results.title: Formula for the isomorphism onto the multiplication dual
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$, let $M$ be a nonzero $A$-submodule of $K$, and let $\varphi \colon \operatorname{Hom}_A(M, A) \to M^\vee$ be the isomorphism onto the dual submodule $M^\vee$ of $M$ for the multiplication form $(x, y) \mapsto xy$ on $K$. results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Dual of a nonzero fractional ideal is its inverse

results.title: The ring $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ of locally integer polynomial functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ is the subring of the ring of all functions $U \to \mathbb{Z}$ (with pointwise operations) consisting of the functions $f$ such that for every finite subset $X \subseteq U$ there is a polynomial $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $p(x) = f(x)$ for all $x \in X$.

results.title: Membership in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and $f : U \to \mathbb{Z}$, $f$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ if and only if for every finite subset $X \subseteq U$ there is a polynomial $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $p(x) = f(x)$ for all $x \in X$.

results.title: The triangular-number function is not LIP on the integers

results.summary: The function $x \mapsto x(x+1)/2$ on $\mathbb{Z}$ (an integer, since $x(x+1)$ is even) does not belong to $\mathrm{LIP}(\mathbb{Z})$: no integer polynomial $p$ takes the values $0, 0, 1$ at $-1, 0, 1$, since $1 - (-1)$ must divide $p(1) - p(-1)$.

results.title: The evaluation map from $\mathbb{Z}(x)$ to $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, the evaluation map is the ring homomorphism from $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ to the ring $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ of locally integer polynomial functions on $U$ that sends each integer polynomial $p$ to the function $U \to \mathbb{Z}$, $u \mapsto p(u)$.

results.title: Interpolation polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be finite and $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. The interpolation polynomial $f_X \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ of $f$ on $X$ is the Lagrange interpolation polynomial: the unique polynomial with rational coefficients of degree less than $|X|$ such that $f_X(x) = f(x)$ for every $x \in X$.

results.title: The interpolation polynomial agrees with the function on its nodes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be finite and $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. The interpolation polynomial $f_X \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ of $f$ on $X$ satisfies $f_X(x) = f(x)$ for every $x \in X$.

results.title: Degree bound for the interpolation polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be finite and $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. The interpolation polynomial $f_X \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ of $f$ on $X$ has degree less than $|X|$, where the zero polynomial has degree $-\infty$.

results.title: Integer polynomials embed in LIP(U)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every infinite set $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, the evaluation map $\mathbb{Z}[x] \to \mathrm{LIP}(U)$, sending $p$ to the function $u \mapsto p(u)$, is injective: distinct integer polynomials give distinct functions on $U$.

results.title: Integrality of low-degree interpolants
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be finite, let $q \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ have degree less than $|X|$, and let $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ satisfy $q(x) = p(x)$ for all $x \in X$. Then $q$ has integer coefficients, that is, $q$ is the image in $\mathbb{Q}[x]$ of a polynomial in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

results.title: A locally integer polynomial function with infinitely many zeros is zero
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Locally integer polynomial functions agreeing on an infinite subset are equal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $U \subseteq V \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $U$ infinite, and let $f, g : V \to \mathbb{Z}$ lie in the ring $\mathrm{LIP}(V)$ of locally integer polynomial functions on $V$. If $f(x) = g(x)$ for every $x \in U$, then $f = g$.

results.title: Intersection of two arithmetic progressions of natural numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a_1, a_2, d_1, d_2$ be natural numbers with $d_1, d_2 > 0$, where $\mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$, and let $P_i = \{a_i + d_i n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ for $i = 1, 2$. Then $P_1 \cap P_2$ is nonempty if and only if $\gcd(d_1, d_2)$ divides the integer $a_1 - a_2$, and if $P_1 \cap P_2$ is nonempty, then $P_1 \cap P_2 = \{a_3 + \operatorname{lcm}(d_1, d_2)\, n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ for some $a_3 \in \mathbb{N}$.
